reports.one_liner: ABB India makes and sells electrification gear (switchgear, panels, power distribution equipment) and industrial automation/motion systems for factories, infrastructure, utilities and data centres; it is 75%-owned by the Swiss-Swedish ABB Group and exited its robotics business in 2026.
tags: Robotics unit sold to group co.

reports.one_liner: Adani Energy Solutions runs India's largest private power transmission network, the Mumbai electricity distribution business (AEML), a fast-growing smart-metering arm, and a newer EPC-style "Energy Solutions Platform".
Adani Enterprises is the Adani Group's incubator company - it builds new businesses (airports, roads, green/new energy, data centres, mining services) and spins them off once they mature.
Adani Green Energy develops and operates large-scale solar, wind and hybrid power plants across India, selling electricity to state utilities and corporates under long-term contracts.
Adani Power is India's largest private thermal power generator, running coal-based plants across several states and recently adding capacity through the Jaiprakash Associates insolvency acquisition.

Ambuja Cements manufactures and sells cement and clinker across India, and is the Adani Group's consolidation platform for its cement business (now absorbing Sanghi, Penna, and in the process of merging with ACC and Orient Cement).
Asian Paints makes and sells decorative and industrial paints, coatings and related home-improvement products, and is India's largest paint company by sales.
Axis Bank is India's third-largest private sector bank, lending to retail, SME and corporate customers and running credit card, wealth and payments businesses alongside deposit-taking.
Bajaj Auto makes two-wheelers (Pulsar, Chetak electric scooter) and three-wheelers in India, and since late 2025 has taken majority control of Austria's KTM through its European subsidiary.

Bajaj Finserv is the Bajaj Group's financial-services holding company, whose value comes mainly from its ~52% stake in Bajaj Finance (consumer lending) plus now-wholly-owned general and life insurance arms.

Bajaj Holdings & Investment is the Bajaj Group's holding company - it owns roughly a third of Bajaj Auto and around 38% of Bajaj Finserv, plus a bond/equity investment portfolio and a small windmill power business, and earns its income mainly from dividends, its share of those two companies' profits, and gains on its portfolio.

Bajaj Finance is India's largest diversified NBFC, lending across consumer durables, personal loans, SME, mortgages, gold loans and rural/urban retail finance through a huge digital and branch network.
Bank of Baroda is a government-owned (PSU) commercial bank that takes deposits and lends to retail, agriculture, MSME and corporate customers across India and roughly 17 other countries.
Bharat Electronics is a Government of India-owned defence electronics company that builds radar, communication, avionics, weapon-control and cybersecurity systems mainly for India's armed forces.
Bharti Airtel is India's second-largest mobile operator, also running towers, home broadband, enterprise data/cloud services, and a majority-owned pan-African mobile business, Airtel Africa.

Bosch Limited is the Indian listed arm of Germany's Bosch Group, making fuel-injection, powertrain and other mobility components for cars, two-wheelers and commercial vehicles, plus an auto-parts aftermarket business.
BPCL is a government-controlled company that imports and refines crude oil and sells petrol, diesel and LPG through its retail network across India.
BSE Ltd runs India's oldest stock exchange, earning fees on equity and derivatives trading, new company listings, and market data/technology services.
Canara Bank is a large government-owned (public sector) bank offering deposits, loans and retail/corporate/agri banking across India.

CG Power makes power transmission and distribution equipment (transformers, switchgear) and industrial products (motors, drives, railway systems), and is now building a new semiconductor packaging (OSAT) business under Murugappa Group ownership.
Cholamandalam Investment and Finance (Murugappa Group) is a diversified NBFC that lends against vehicles, homes/property and small businesses, and also runs a general insurance joint venture.

Cipla is an Indian pharmaceutical company making generic medicines, branded formulations and APIs, with a sizeable respiratory and peptide pipeline sold across India, the US, South Africa and other emerging markets.
Coal India is the world's largest coal miner, a government-controlled company that digs and sells thermal coal mostly to Indian power plants.
Cummins India makes diesel and natural gas engines and generator sets, selling to domestic power, industrial and rail customers while exporting engines to its US parent, Cummins Inc.

Divi's Laboratories makes active pharmaceutical ingredients, custom-synthesis (CDMO) intermediates for global pharma and agrochemical companies, and nutraceuticals, selling mostly to customers outside India.

DLF is India's largest listed real-estate developer, building and selling homes (mostly luxury, concentrated around Gurugram) while also earning steady rental income from offices and malls through its DCCDL joint venture.
DMart (Avenue Supermarts) runs a chain of value-format supermarkets and hypermarkets selling groceries, FMCG, general merchandise and apparel, mostly out of stores it owns rather than leases.
Dr. Reddy's Laboratories is an Indian pharmaceutical company making generic drugs, active pharma ingredients and biosimilars, sold mainly in the US, India, Russia/CIS and other emerging markets.

Siemens Energy India makes and services power transmission and generation equipment - transformers, switchgear, and gas/steam turbines - for utilities and industry, having been carved out of Siemens Limited in a 2024 demerger.

Eternal Limited (renamed from Zomato) runs online food delivery (Zomato), quick-commerce grocery delivery (Blinkit), a going-out/bookings app (District) and a B2B food-supply business (Hyperpure) under one listed entity.
GAIL (India) Ltd runs the country's largest natural gas transmission pipeline network and trades gas, while also running petrochemical, LPG, and LNG businesses.
Godrej Consumer Products makes household and personal-care staples - soaps, hair colour, air fresheners, insecticides - sold mainly in India, Indonesia, Africa and Latin America.

Grasim is an Aditya Birla Group conglomerate whose own business is viscose fibre and chemicals, but most of its market value sits in its controlling stakes in UltraTech Cement and Aditya Birla Capital, plus newer paints and B2B e-commerce ventures.
HCL Technologies is an IT services, engineering and digital transformation company that builds and runs software and technology systems for large corporate clients worldwide.
HDFC AMC runs HDFC Mutual Fund, earning fees as a percentage of the money it manages across equity, debt and other schemes.
HDFC Bank is India's largest private-sector lender, taking deposits and lending across retail, corporate and (since absorbing parent HDFC Ltd in 2023) home loans.
HDFC Life sells life insurance policies - term, savings/endowment, ULIP, pension and group products - distributed mainly through HDFC Bank branches and other bancassurance and agency channels.
HUL makes and sells everyday consumer products in India — soaps, detergents, shampoos, skincare, tea/coffee and packaged foods — and is majority owned by Unilever plc.
Hindustan Zinc, majority-owned by Vedanta, is India's largest integrated zinc-lead-silver miner and refiner, running mines and smelters mainly in Rajasthan plus a wind power business.
ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private sector bank, taking deposits and lending across retail, SME, corporate and rural segments, with insurance and asset-management subsidiaries alongside.

Vodafone Idea is India's third-largest mobile telecom operator, a joint venture of UK's Vodafone Group and India's Aditya Birla Group, now majority-owned by the Government of India after unpaid licence dues were converted into equity.
IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) is India's largest airline by passengers carried, running a low-cost domestic and international flight network.

Infosys is an Indian IT services and consulting company that runs technology operations, software development and maintenance for global clients, and is now pushing AI-driven automation into that work.
Indian Oil Corporation is India's largest state-run oil company, refining crude oil and marketing petrol, diesel, LPG and other fuels across the country.

IRFC raises money from the markets and leases railway rolling stock (and increasingly, other infrastructure assets) back to Indian Railways and other public-sector borrowers, earning a thin, regulated margin on a very large loan book.

ITC is a diversified Indian conglomerate whose profit is still dominated by cigarettes, alongside a fast-growing packaged foods and personal care business, paperboard/packaging, and agri-trading; it demerged its hotels business into a separately listed company in January 2025.

Jindal Steel Limited (formerly Jindal Steel & Power) makes steel in Chhattisgarh and Odisha, selling plates, rails, structural steel and other long/flat products, and is mid-way through a large capacity expansion at its Angul plant.

Jio Financial Services is the Reliance-promoted financial holding company housing an NBFC (Jio Credit), a payments bank, insurance distribution/JV stakes, and asset and wealth management joint ventures with BlackRock.
JSW Steel is one of India's largest integrated steel makers, producing flat and long steel products from plants in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha and overseas (US, with JV capacity in India too).

reports.one_liner: Kotak Mahindra Bank is a private-sector lender that, with its banking and non-banking subsidiaries, runs loans, deposits, insurance distribution, asset management and broking across India.

L&T is India's largest engineering & construction conglomerate, executing large infrastructure, power, defence and hydrocarbon projects, while also holding stakes in separately listed IT services (LTIMindtree, L&T Technology Services) and financial services (L&T Finance) businesses.
LTM Limited (formerly LTIMindtree, renamed March 2026) is an IT and digital/AI consulting services company formed from the L&T Infotech-Mindtree merger, majority-owned by Larsen & Toubro.

Mahindra & Mahindra manufactures utility vehicles (Thar, XUV700, Scorpio, and newer electric SUVs) and is the world's largest tractor maker by volume, with sizeable stakes in financial services (Mahindra Finance) and IT services (Tech Mahindra) alongside the core auto and farm business.
Maruti Suzuki is India's largest passenger car maker, majority owned by Japan's Suzuki Motor Corporation, making small cars, SUVs and CNG vehicles for the domestic market and export.

Max Healthcare Institute runs a network of multi-specialty hospitals concentrated in Delhi-NCR and North India, offering tertiary and quaternary care in areas like oncology, cardiac sciences and transplants.
Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is a Mumbai-based, government-owned shipyard that builds warships and submarines for the Indian Navy under long-term defence contracts.
Samvardhana Motherson makes auto parts for carmakers worldwide - wiring harnesses, mirrors, plastic modules - and is now pushing into aerospace and consumer electronics through acquisitions.
tags: Q1 FY26 profit fell 45% on tariff lag

reports.one_liner: Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold-loan NBFC, lending against pledged household gold jewellery, with microfinance, housing and vehicle-loan units alongside the core gold business.
Nestle India makes and sells packaged foods and beverages - Maggi noodles, Nescafe, KitKat, baby food and dairy products - and is majority owned by Swiss parent Nestle S.A.

NTPC is India's largest power generator, a government-owned utility running coal-fired thermal plants plus a fast-growing renewable arm (NTPC Green Energy), selling power to state distribution companies under regulated, cost-plus tariffs.

ONGC is India's largest oil and gas exploration and production company, a government-controlled PSU that extracts crude oil and natural gas domestically and holds stakes in refining/petrochemical arms like MRPL, HPCL and OPaL.

PFC is a government-owned (Navratna) NBFC that provides long-term project finance to power generation, transmission and distribution companies across India, and now also owns and consolidates REC Limited as its subsidiary.
Punjab National Bank is India's second-largest government-owned bank, taking deposits and lending to retail, agriculture, MSME and corporate borrowers across the country.
Polycab is India's largest wires-and-cables manufacturer, with a growing side business in fans, switches and appliances (FMEG) and a smaller EPC/EHV cable-projects arm.
Power Grid Corporation is the Indian government-owned monopoly that builds and operates most of India's inter-state electricity transmission network, earning regulated tariffs on its asset base.

Hitachi Energy India (formerly ABB Power Products and Systems India) makes power transmission and distribution equipment — transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems and grid automation — for utilities, industry, data centres and renewable energy projects in India.
Reliance Industries is India's largest company by revenue, a conglomerate spanning oil refining and petrochemicals (O2C), telecom (Jio), retail, and new energy.
SBI Life Insurance sells life insurance, savings, protection, pension and group policies across India, distributing mainly through SBI's bank branches and its own agency force.

SBI is India's largest bank by assets, a majority government-owned lender offering retail and corporate banking, deposits and credit, alongside subsidiaries in life insurance, cards and asset management.
Shriram Finance is India's largest non-bank lender (NBFC), built on financing used and new commercial vehicles, with gold loans, MSME and personal loans as newer additions.

Siemens Ltd makes industrial automation, digital-industries and smart-infrastructure (building/electrical) equipment and rail mobility systems in India, after spinning off its power/energy equipment business as a separately listed Siemens Energy India in April 2025.
tags: Raw -22% drawdown is a demerger illusion

reports.one_liner: Solar Industries India makes industrial explosives and detonators for mining and infrastructure, and has rapidly scaled into defence ordnance, missile systems and ammunition for Indian and export customers.

Sun Pharma is India's largest pharmaceutical company, selling generic drugs alongside a growing specialty/innovative portfolio (dermatology, oncology, ophthalmology) in India, the US and over 100 other countries.
Tata Capital is the Tata Group's diversified non-bank lender, financing retail, SME, corporate, housing and vehicle loans, and now entering gold loans.

Tata Consumer Products sells packaged tea, coffee and salt (Tata Tea, Tetley, Tata Salt) plus a growing foods basket - Sampann, Ching's Secret, Soulfull, Organic India - in India and abroad, and holds a 50:50 stake in Tata Starbucks cafes.

Tata Power is an integrated power company that generates (coal, hydro, renewables), transmits and distributes electricity, and is now expanding into EV charging and grid infrastructure for data centres.

Tata Steel is an integrated steel producer with large operations in India (Kalinganagar, Jamshedpur) and in Europe (Netherlands, UK), selling steel to construction, auto, infrastructure and retail customers.
TCS is India's largest IT services company, running outsourced software development, IT infrastructure and AI-led digital transformation projects for large global clients.
Tech Mahindra is a Mahindra Group IT services and BPO company that runs telecom, manufacturing, BFSI and other enterprise clients' technology and network operations.
Titan Company, part of the Tata Group, sells jewellery (Tanishq, CaratLane, Mia, Zoya), watches and eyewear through India's largest organised retail network for these categories.

Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Ltd) makes trucks, buses, pickups and other commercial vehicles — it is the standalone CV business that was demerged from the erstwhile Tata Motors in November 2025, leaving passenger cars and JLR in a separate entity (TMPV).
Makes and sells Tata-brand cars, EVs and CNG vehicles in India and owns Jaguar Land Rover in the UK, after demerging its commercial-vehicle business into a separately listed company in October 2025.

Torrent Pharmaceuticals makes branded generic medicines for India and export markets like Brazil and Germany, and since January 2026 has absorbed JB Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals, adding a US-generics and contract manufacturing business.
Trent runs Tata Group's fashion and retail chains in India - the budget-fashion chain Zudio, the mid-premium Westside, and grocery/beauty formats like Star Bazaar and Zudio-adjacent Samoh/Misbu.

TVS Motor makes and sells two-wheelers, three-wheelers and electric two-wheelers in India and over 80 export markets, with an in-house NBFC (TVS Credit) that finances a large chunk of its retail sales.

UltraTech Cement is India's largest cement maker (part of the Aditya Birla Group), producing cement, ready-mix concrete and construction chemicals from a capacity base that has swelled past 190 MTPA after recent acquisitions.
Union Bank of India is a government-owned public sector bank that takes deposits and lends to corporates, retail borrowers, agriculture and MSMEs across India.

Vedanta Aluminium Metal Limited (VAML) runs India's largest integrated aluminium business - the Lanjigarh alumina refinery, the giant Jharsuguda smelter, and a 51% stake in BALCO - after being demerged out of Vedanta Ltd and listed separately in June 2026.

Varun Beverages is PepsiCo's largest bottling franchisee outside the US, manufacturing and distributing packaged drinks (and increasingly snacks) across India and a fast-growing set of international markets including South Africa, Zimbabwe, Kenya and Central Asia.

Vedanta Ltd is now the 'residual' post-demerger entity centred on a ~63% stake in Hindustan Zinc plus its own zinc-international, copper and ferro-chrome operations, after its aluminium, power, oil & gas, and iron & steel businesses were spun off into four separately listed companies in 2026.
Wipro is an Indian IT services and consulting company that builds, runs and modernises technology systems for large global corporations across banking, healthcare, manufacturing and other sectors.
Zydus Lifesciences makes generic and branded medicines for the US and Indian markets, plus consumer wellness products and specialty/biosimilar drugs.
